standards_referenced: S725_SESSION_SCAN_METHODOLOGY_STANDARD.md — AM-1 through AM-3, FM-001 through FM-008
S726_RULE2_PARSE_SPEC.md — AM-1 Function constructor parse specification
SESSION201_IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.json — compound key model, dual-block architecture

meta.mandatory_methodology: AM-1 Function Constructor Parse (per S725 §2 + S726 §3)
forbidden_methodologies: FM-001: Forward-scan regex for CC from QID anchor
FM-004: Flat field-name regex without object-boundary awareness
FM-005: Totals-only defect reports without QID lists
FM-006: Remediation script without pre/post defect cross-scan
FM-007: Agent self-report reliance without independent verification
FM-008: Session closure without CURRENT_BASELINES.md update
meta.core_principle: Within-object extraction ONLY — CorrectChoice and ExplanationWrong[A-D] must come from the SAME brace-delimited object. QID-only targeting is prohibited.
meta.identity_precondition: Gate -1 is mandatory — no downstream scan result is admissible until IDENTITY_VALID (S202 Amendment 1).

group_identity.purpose: Establish item identity before any structural or content scan

group_structural.purpose: Detect field-level structural defects — field presence, emptiness, format

group_content.purpose: Detect content-quality defects in explanation text — boilerplate, missing citations

group_metadata.purpose: Verify metadata completeness, consistency, and taxonomy compliance

group_certification.purpose: Verify answer-key correctness, difficulty calibration, and readiness for delivery

scans.title: Identity Validation — QID Presence, CC Presence, Pack Attribution, TemplateFamily Constructibility
scans.purpose: Verify every item has a constructible identity before any structural or content scan runs. This is the mandatory identity pre-condition. S320 proved: wrong target + perfect scan = wrong result.
inputs: Raw pack file content for all 5 packs (pack_a_corrected.js through pack_e_corrected.js)
Per-pack QID format regex rules
Cross-pack QID comparison baselines

algorithm.step1_qid_validation: For every item in every pack: verify QuestionID exists, matches expected pack format (Pack A: P1-{S}-{NNN}, Pack B: P1B-{S}-{NNN}, Pack C: P1-{S}C-{NNN} or P1-{S}-{NNN}, Pack D: P1-{S}D-{NNN}, Pack E: P1E-{S}-{NNN})
algorithm.step2_cc_validation: Verify CorrectChoice field exists, is a single character A-D, and is extracted from the SAME brace-delimited object as QuestionID
algorithm.step3_pack_attribution: Verify the item's file path matches its configured pack. Self-check: for each item, confirm that scanning forward/backward from its QuestionID does NOT find the same QID in a different pack file
algorithm.step4_template_family: For each item: compute stem Jaccard similarity (proper-noun-removed) against all other items in the same section. Classify into rotation groups (>90% stem similarity + same choice texts positioned rotationally) or confirm standalone (<70% similarity). Flag unclassifiable items (70-90%) as IDENTITY_WARN.
algorithm.step5_compound_key_generation: For every item: generate compound key as QID + CorrectChoice + pack_file_path. Verify uniqueness across all 5 packs.

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If QID missing → IDENTITY_BLOCKED (item excluded from all downstream gates). If CC missing → IDENTITY_BLOCKED. If unclassifiable → IDENTITY_WARN (item proceeds but flagged). If Function constructor parse fails → IDENTITY_FATAL (entire pack excluded; escalate to governance).
scans.blocking_rationale: Per S202 Amendment 1: no downstream scan result is admissible until IDENTITY_VALID. DL-008, DL-026, DL-013, and DL-016 scans produce unusable results when run against items with broken identity.
scans.false_positive_risk: LOW — QID/CC presence and format are deterministic. TemplateFamily Jaccard clustering at >90% threshold produces clean separation between rotation families. Edge case: boundary items at 70-90% similarity flagged as IDENTITY_WARN for human review.
scans.implementation_complexity: MEDIUM — QID/CC/pack checks are trivial (~40 lines). TemplateFamily clustering requires proper-noun stripping + stem Jaccard + group-threshold clustering (~60 lines). Cross-pack collision check requires loading all 5 packs simultaneously. Total ~150 lines.

scans.title: JSON Integrity — Parseability, Field Presence, Corruption Detection, Count Verification
scans.purpose: Verify all pack and case files are parseable, structurally complete, and free of known corruption. This gate must pass before any downstream structural or content scan can operate.
inputs: Raw pack file content (5 pack files + 5 scored_cases files)
Function constructor parse capability
Expected question counts per pack (500 each for packs A-E, 90 for scored_cases.js, 300 for scored_cases2-5 combined)
Corruption pattern catalog (DL-017 backtick-newline, orphaned braces/commas, duplicate QIDs)

algorithm.step1_parse: Function constructor parse of full pack array. Extract variable name from `const MCQ_BANK_{X} = [` pattern. Execute `new Function(fileContent + '; return ' + varName + ';')`. If parse fails → attempt AM-2 string-aware brace-matched extraction of individual objects. If THAT fails → HARD_BLOCK with error report showing line numbers and failure reason.
algorithm.step2_field_presence: For each parsed object, verify all required fields exist: QuestionID, Stem, Choices (or Choices.{A,B,C,D}), CorrectChoice, ExplanationCorrect, ExplanationWrongA, ExplanationWrongB, ExplanationWrongC, ExplanationWrongD. Missing required fields → flag.
algorithm.step3_type_consistency: Verify CorrectChoice is a single letter A-D. Verify ExplanationWrong fields are strings (or empty strings). Verify question_state (if present) is one of the 5 valid values.
algorithm.step4_corruption_detection: Scan for known corruption artifacts: `\x60n` (DL-017 backtick-newline), `,NNN: true,` (DL-017 duplicate artifact), unmatched braces, orphaned commas, duplicate QuestionIDs within same pack.
algorithm.step5_count_verification: Verify parse-count matches expected pack size (Pack A: 500, Pack B: 500, Pack C: 500, Pack D: 500, Pack E: 500). Cross-validate against `grep -c '"QuestionID"'` on source file. Discrepancy → HARD_BLOCK.

scans.fail_safe_behavior: Unparseable file → HARD_BLOCK entire pipeline for that file. Missing required fields → HARD_BLOCK affected items. Corruption detected → HARD_BLOCK (remediation required before re-run). Count mismatch → HARD_BLOCK (investigate before proceeding).
scans.blocking_rationale: If the file cannot be parsed, no downstream gate can operate. If required fields are missing, structural and content scans will crash or produce unreliable results.
scans.false_positive_risk: LOW — parse failures are deterministic. Field-presence checks are deterministic. Corruption artifact matching had 0 false positives on DL-017. QuestionID count is deterministic. Only fuzzy area: type-consistency for edge-case numeric-format CorrectChoice fields.
scans.implementation_complexity: MEDIUM — Step 1 (parse) reuses ExplanationValidator.extractQuestions pattern. Step 4 (corruption detection) requires maintaining a catalog of known corruption patterns. Step 5 requires per-pack expected-count mapping.

scans.title: ExplanationWrong[CorrectChoice] Non-Empty
scans.purpose: Detect EV8 violations: the ExplanationWrong slot matching CorrectChoice is non-empty. This is the highest-priority learner-safety defect — wrong text appears in the correct-answer review slot.
inputs: Parsed question objects (AM-1 Function constructor output) with CorrectChoice and ExplanationWrong[A-D] fields

algorithm.step1_extract: For each parsed question object q: read cc = q.CorrectChoice. If !cc → skip.
algorithm.step2_check: Access ewVal = q['ExplanationWrong' + cc]. If ewVal !== undefined && ewVal !== null && String(ewVal).trim().length > 0 → VIOLATION.
algorithm.step3_record: Record QuestionID, CorrectChoice, field name, value excerpt (first 100 chars), length, question_state. Must include QID list — totals-only output is PROHIBITED per FM-005.
algorithm.step4_cross_validate: Co-detect DL-018 (absent EW[CC] field): if q['ExplanationWrong' + cc] is undefined → flag DL-018 separately. Co-detect DL-026 within same pass: for each non-CC letter, if EW[letter] === '' → flag DL-026.

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If Function constructor parse fails → fall back to AM-2 string-aware brace-matched parse. If no parse method succeeds → report PARSE_FAILED and return empty (do NOT guess). Never use FM-001 forward-scan as fallback.
scans.blocking_rationale: Items with non-empty EW[CC] display wrong-answer text where the correct-answer explanation should appear. Per CAQS §4.4 EV8 and governance-guard Rule 2 (BLOCK level).
scans.false_positive_risk: LOW — 0% false positive rate across 539 historical occurrences. Every flag was a genuine EV8 violation when using within-object extraction. DL-029 CC-offset artifacts are eliminated by within-object extraction.
scans.implementation_complexity: LOW — Single-pass object extraction + field access + string length test. ~20 lines of JavaScript. Reuses governance-guard.js extractObjectsFromText pattern upgraded to AM-1.
scans.gold_standard_test: Pack B must return 0 DL-008. Any scan returning >0 on Pack B is non-compliant per S725 §6.2.

scans.title: Correct-Answer Slot in ExplanationWrong Fields Must Be Empty
scans.purpose: Same as DL-008 detection but extended to case-study items. EV8 is the CAQS rule; DL-008 is the defect classification. Single scan serves both.
inputs: Parsed MCQ question objects (AM-1 output)
Parsed case-study item objects (scored_cases*.js, AM-1 or AM-2 parsed)

outputs.mcq: Same as PG-001 output — combined DL-008/EV8 report

algorithm.mcq_path: Identical to PG-001 — same pass, zero additional runtime
algorithm.case_path: For each item in scored_cases*.js: if item.Type is 'select' or 'multi' and item has Choices array, identify the correct-answer index from item.Correct. Verify the corresponding slot in the explanation fields (case items use different field naming — adapt detection to case structure).

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If case-item parse fails → flag CASE_PARSE_FAILED, skip case items, proceed with MCQ results only.
scans.blocking_rationale: Same as DL-008 — per CAQS §4.4 EV8 and governance-guard Rule 2.
scans.false_positive_risk: LOW — case items have not been systematically scanned for EV8 but use parallel field structure. Within-object extraction eliminates CC-offset artifacts.
scans.implementation_complexity: LOW — Reuses PG-001 implementation. Extension to case items requires field-name mapping adaptation. ~20 additional lines.

scans.title: Empty or Absent Non-CorrectChoice ExplanationWrong Slots
scans.purpose: Detect three defect classes in a single pass: (a) DL-026: Empty string at non-CC EW slot, (b) DL-025: Empty string at non-CC EW slot in Pack A only (historical subset), (c) DL-021: Structurally absent EW field at non-CC position (Pack E Section C pattern, more severe).
inputs: Parsed question objects (AM-1 output) with CorrectChoice and all 4 ExplanationWrong fields from SAME object boundary

algorithm.step1_extract: For each parsed question object q: read cc = q.CorrectChoice.
algorithm.step2_iterate_slots: For each letter L in {A, B, C, D}: if L === cc → check DL-008 (EW[CC] non-empty → separate violation). If L !== cc → check field: (a) if !(('ExplanationWrong' + L) in q) → DL-021 absent-field violation. (b) if q['ExplanationWrong' + L] === '' → DL-026 empty-slot violation. (c) if q['ExplanationWrong' + L] is non-empty string < 50 chars → EV1 minimum-length violation.
algorithm.step3_cross_validate_dl016: If DL-016 is active on this item (metadata-block ChoiceA-D differs from content-block Choices.A-D), flag the DL-026 finding as POTENTIALLY_DL016_ARTIFACT and require human verification before remediation.
algorithm.step4_distinguish_dl021_from_dl018: DL-021 = absent EW field at NON-CC position (3 distractor slots); DL-018 = absent EW field at CC position (1 slot). Track separately.

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If parsed object has no ExplanationWrong fields at all → flag INCOMPLETE_OBJECT (possible parse artifact). If CC is absent → cannot assess; skip item with UNKNOWN_CC flag.
scans.blocking_rationale: Empty distractor slots mean learners receive zero educational feedback when they select certain wrong answers. Per CAQS §4.3 (Choice-specific explanations required) and CAQS §4.4 EV1.
scans.false_positive_risk: MEDIUM — DL-016 metadata-content mismatch can cause scan false positives when EW fields exist in Block 2 but appear absent from Block 1 perspective. Cross-validate all DL-026 flags against DL-016 status — items with BOTH DL-016 AND DL-026 may have DL-026 as a scan artifact.
scans.implementation_complexity: LOW — Same pass as DL-008. The ExplanationValidator.js line 173 guard must be replaced with a check that distinguishes CC-slots (DL-008) from non-CC-slots (DL-026/DL-021). ~15-line modification.

scans.title: Metadata-Block vs Content-Block Choice Divergence
scans.purpose: Detect when the metadata-block ChoiceA-D text differs from the content-block Choices.{A,B,C,D} text. This defect causes ExplanationWrong fields to describe the wrong item's distractors (DL-016 +1 offset).
inputs: Parsed question objects with BOTH flat ChoiceA-D fields AND nested Choices.{A,B,C,D} fields extracted from the SAME object boundary

algorithm.step1_dual_block_detection: For each parsed object: check if BOTH flat ChoiceA-D AND nested Choices.{A,B,C,D} exist. If only one format exists → single-object architecture (Pack B, Pack E); skip DL-016 check.
algorithm.step2_field_comparison: Compare pairwise: ChoiceA vs Choices.A, ChoiceB vs Choices.B, ChoiceC vs Choices.C, ChoiceD vs Choices.D. If ANY pair differs → flag DL-016 structural divergence.
algorithm.step3_rotation_offset_verification: For items with divergence: compute EW-to-choice lexical overlap. If EW in slot L has >50% lexical overlap with choice L+1 (rotation neighbor) but <20% with choice L → confirm +1 rotation offset pattern.
algorithm.step4_certification_block: If item is Certified AND has DL-016 divergence → mark as learner-safety CRITICAL. Per G-NEW-1/G-NEW-3: certification is blocked until blocks are aligned.

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If object has only one choice format → skip DL-016 (not applicable — single-object architecture). If both formats exist but one path is corrupted → flag as DL016_PARSE_WARN requiring manual field inspection.
scans.blocking_rationale: Items with confirmed DL-016 deliver wrong-topic distractor feedback. Per QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md §9.4.2 G-NEW-1/G-NEW-3: the content block is the authoritative source of truth.
scans.false_positive_risk: LOW — Structural divergence (ChoiceA != Choices.A) has 0% historical false positive rate. If the two fields exist and differ, it is a genuine divergence. Edge case: when one field exists and the other is absent → flag as WARN, not HARD_BLOCK.
scans.implementation_complexity: MEDIUM — Requires dual-field-path extraction (flat + nested fields from same object). Must handle absent fields gracefully (not all items have both formats). ~80 lines.

scans.title: Boilerplate Distractor Explanations
scans.purpose: Detect template-generated generic distractor explanation text that provides no choice-specific educational value.
inputs: Parsed question objects with ExplanationWrong[A-D] field values

algorithm.pattern_dl013_classic: Regex match within each EW field for presence of BOTH 'represents a plausible misconception' AND 'A candidate may select this option by misapplying' → classic DL-013 boilerplate.
algorithm.pattern_dl027_closing_tag: Regex match for 'A candidate selecting this option may misunderstand how the governing standard applies to this specific fact pattern' → DL-027 closing-tag variant.
algorithm.pattern_ew_duplicate: Within each item: compute Jaccard similarity between every pair of ExplanationWrong fields. If any pair exceeds 80% similarity → near-identical template text across distractor slots. Flag as DL-013 variant.
algorithm.pattern_placeholder: Regex match for known placeholder phrases from ExplanationValidator.js placeholderPatterns: 'This is the correct choice', 'Plausible distractor', 'Incorrect choice', 'Common misunderstanding'.

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If EW field is absent (DL-021/DL-018) → skip content check for that slot. If field is empty (DL-026) → skip. Report DL-013 count separately from DL-026/DL-021 structural counts.
scans.blocking_rationale: DL-013 boilerplate is NOT a learner-safety risk (text is directionally correct). It blocks certification because it fails CAQS §4.3 (Choice-specific) and EV4. SOFT_BLOCK = certification deferred until remediated, but existing Certified items are not retroactively decertified.
scans.false_positive_risk: LOW — Pattern A (dual-phrase regex) had 0% false positive rate across 2,587 occurrences. Pattern B (Jaccard >80% across slots) may produce rare false positives when two distractors genuinely share vocabulary. Pattern A = HARD evidence; Pattern B = WARN for human review.
scans.implementation_complexity: LOW — Regex pattern matching is trivial (~10 lines). Jaccard similarity is standard. Extend ExplanationValidator placeholderPatterns array. ~25 lines.

scans.title: ExplanationCorrect Missing Accounting Principle Reference
scans.purpose: Verify ExplanationCorrect text references the governing accounting principle by name (CAQS §4.3: 'Correct answer must reference the accounting principle by name'). Co-detects DL-009: wrong standard citation for the topic.
inputs: Parsed question objects with ExplanationCorrect text and Topic field

algorithm.step1_citation_regex: Scan ExplanationCorrect for known standard citation patterns: ASC \d{3}(-\d{2}(-\d{2})?)?, IAS \d{1,2}, IFRS \d{1,2}, COSO, GAAP, FASB, 'IMA Statement', 'Sarbanes-Oxley', SEC, PCAOB, AICPA. If NO patterns match → flag EV3.
algorithm.step2_citation_topic_match: If citation exists but standard scope does not match the item's Topic → flag DL-009. Cross-reference against known-good topic→standard mapping (e.g., loss contingencies → ASC 450, not ASC 210; goodwill impairment → ASC 350, not ASC 360).
algorithm.step3_nonsensical_citation: Detect template-placeholder citations like 'Artificial intelligence in accounting' as the governing standard for cost-management topics. Flag as SEVERE DL-009.

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If ExplanationCorrect is absent or shorter than 50 chars → flag EC_SHORT (EV1 violation) separately from EV3.
scans.blocking_rationale: Missing principle citation degrades educational quality but does not create learner-safety risk (answer is still correct). CAQS §4.3 makes this mandatory for Gold Standard but not basic certification.
scans.false_positive_risk: MEDIUM — Some legitimate explanations reference standards by description rather than code (e.g., 'Under generally accepted accounting principles...'). Conversely, passing mentions of ASC codes may not satisfy EV3 intent. Recommended: flag as WARN, not automated block.
scans.implementation_complexity: LOW — Pure regex pattern matching. Add regex array to ExplanationValidator. ~15 lines. DL-009 cross-reference requires a topic→standard mapping table (~50 entries).

scans.title: Misassigned Choice Explanations
scans.purpose: Detect when ExplanationWrong text semantically describes a choice other than the one it is assigned to. This is an inherently semantic defect requiring NLP/human review.
inputs: Parsed question objects with Choices.{A,B,C,D} and ExplanationWrong[A-D] from SAME object boundary (content-block choice comparison, not metadata-block — avoids DL-016 contamination)

algorithm.tier1_lexical_overlap: For each EW slot L: compute Jaccard similarity between ExplanationWrong[L] text and Choices.{L} text. Flag if similarity < 15% (EW text has no lexical relationship to its assigned choice). Uses content-block Choices.{A,B,C,D} as ground truth, NOT metadata-block ChoiceA-D.
algorithm.tier2_numeric_drift: Extract numeric values (dollar amounts, ratios, quantities) from both EW text and Choices. Compare: if EW text describes a numeric result matching Choice B's value but is assigned to slot A → flag DL-010.
algorithm.tier3_ec_cc_cross_check: Cross-validate against ExplanationCorrect: if EC text uses language that matches a specific choice letter, verify that CorrectChoice matches. If EC describes Choice B's reasoning but CC points to Choice C → flag BOTH DL-010 and DL-030.
algorithm.tier4_dl016_interference_guard: If item has DL-016 (metadata-content divergence), SKIP Tier 1 lexical overlap (the comparison targets are wrong). Report item as DL010_UNASSESSABLE until DL-016 is resolved.

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If lexical overlap produces <5% for all 3 non-CC slots AND DL-016 is active → report as DL016_MASKED (cannot assess DL-010 until DL-016 resolved). If numeric extraction fails (non-numeric item) → skip Tier 2, proceed to Tier 3 only.
scans.blocking_rationale: Cannot auto-block certification — high FP risk (~93.9% historically per 2,038 raw findings yielding 125 true positives). Items flagged as WARN must receive human editorial review before certification.
scans.false_positive_risk: HIGH — 93.9% historical false-positive rate. Lexical overlap alone is insufficient discriminant. Full semantic verification requires AI-assisted review. Primary value: screening tool to prioritize human review queue.
scans.implementation_complexity: MEDIUM — Tier 1 (Jaccard) is straightforward (~30 lines). Tier 2 (numeric extraction) requires regex for dollar amounts/percentages (~20 lines). Tier 3 (EC-CC cross-check) requires NLP similarity (~40 lines). Tier 4 (DL-016 guard) requires cross-scan reference.

scans.title: Definition-Match Difficulty Inflation
scans.purpose: Detect items where the question stem is a textbook definition and the correct answer is the defined term, but the item is labeled Moderate/Difficult instead of Easy. Systematic ~500 items estimated.
inputs: Parsed question objects with Stem, Choices.{A,B,C,D}, CorrectChoice, DifficultyScore, CognitiveLevel

algorithm.step1_stem_cc_overlap: Compute Jaccard lexical overlap between Stem text (stop-words removed) and the CorrectChoice's corresponding Choices text. Threshold: >50% overlap triggers DL-031 flag.
algorithm.step2_difficulty_check: If stem-CC overlap >50% AND DifficultyScore >= 3 AND CognitiveLevel is Remember/Understand → flag DL-031 (definition-match over-labeled).
algorithm.step3_distractor_verification: Verify that at least 2 distractors require application-level discernment (>40% Jaccard overlap with their own choice text indicates definition-level). If distractors are also definition-level → confirm inflation. If distractors require genuine discrimination → reduce severity to WARN (difficulty MAY be appropriate).
algorithm.step4_cognitive_cross_check: If CognitiveLevel is 'Apply' or higher but stem-CC overlap >50% → flag BOTH DL-031 (difficulty inflation) AND cognitive-level mismatch.

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If CognitiveLevel field is absent → flag COGNITIVE_LEVEL_MISSING and skip DL-031 check for that item. If DifficultyScore is absent → flag DIFFICULTY_SCORE_MISSING.
scans.blocking_rationale: Difficulty miscalibration does not create learner-safety risk (answer is correct). It degrades psychometric quality and distorts blueprint coverage reporting. WARN = flag for recalibration during certification review.
scans.false_positive_risk: MEDIUM — Jaccard alone is insufficient. Some items with high stem-CC overlap have sophisticated distractor engineering that justifies Moderate labeling. The secondary distractor check reduces FP risk but cannot eliminate it. Final calibration decision requires human judgment.
scans.implementation_complexity: LOW — Jaccard similarity function + threshold comparison + DifficultyScore/CognitiveLevel field check. ~50 lines total.

scans.title: CorrectChoice Answer-Key Errors
scans.purpose: Detect items where the stored CorrectChoice disagrees with the independently derived correct answer. This is the highest-severity defect class — wrong answer marked correct.
inputs: Parsed question objects with Stem, Choices.{A,B,C,D}, CorrectChoice, ExplanationCorrect
FORMULA_MASTER.md — 34 canonical formula templates for Tier 1 numeric verification
Build-time AI — for Tier 2 conceptual verification

algorithm.tier1_numeric_formula_verification: For items with known formula templates: extract numeric values from Stem + Choices. Apply formula from FORMULA_MASTER.md. Compute independently. Compare to stored Correct. Flag mismatch > tolerance. Confidence: HIGH for exact matches, MEDIUM for within-tolerance but wrong formula.
algorithm.tier2_conceptual_ai_verification: For conceptual items: present stem + all 4 choices to build-time AI accounting reviewer. AI independently derives correct answer. Compare to stored CorrectChoice. Flag disagreement. Confidence: HIGH for unambiguous standards (ASC 606, COSO), MEDIUM for judgment areas (relevant costing, transfer pricing).
algorithm.tier3_ec_cc_consistency: Cross-check CorrectChoice against ExplanationCorrect text: does EC text describe the choice that CorrectChoice points to? If EC describes a different choice's reasoning → flag. This catches 3 of 5 known DL-030 items (conceptual design errors where template assigned CC to wrong letter).
algorithm.verdict_scale: ALL_AGREE → pass. AI_DISAGREES → REQUIRES_HUMAN_REVIEW (SOFT_BLOCK). EC_CC_MISMATCH → REQUIRES_HUMAN_REVIEW (SOFT_BLOCK). FORMULA_MISMATCH → CONFIRMED_ERROR (CRITICAL).

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If FORMULA_MASTER.md not found → skip Tier 1; proceed to Tier 3 only. If build-time AI unavailable → skip Tier 2; proceed to Tier 1 + Tier 3 only. NEVER auto-change CorrectChoice based on scan output — all changes require human confirmation.
scans.blocking_rationale: Cannot HARD_BLOCK on automated verification — AI may be wrong about the correct answer. SOFT_BLOCK = item flagged for mandatory human expert review before certification.
scans.false_positive_risk: HIGH — Tier 1 (numeric formula) has LOW FP for items matching known formulas. Tier 2 (conceptual AI) has HIGH FP — AI may derive a different but also defensible answer. Tier 3 (EC-CC cross-check) has MEDIUM FP. All detection is advisory — final CC change requires human confirmation.
scans.implementation_complexity: HIGH — Tier 1 requires formula-template library mapped to item topics. Tier 2 requires build-time AI integration with accounting expertise. Tier 3 requires NLP/semantic comparison. Multi-component architecture. Recommend: Tier 3 first (catches 3/5 known DL-030), then Tier 1, then Tier 2.

scans.title: Template Rotation Group Detection and Seed Identification
scans.purpose: Identify all 5-item template rotation groups across all packs. Classify each group member as seed (canonical) or clone (derivative). Detect rotation pattern consistency (A→B→C→D→A cycle). Provide input to DL-012 archival decisions.
inputs: Parsed question objects (AM-1) for all 5 packs
Per-section seed criteria: Unprocessed, CorrectChoice cycle starts at A, ExplanationCorrect >= 200 chars, EC contains ASC/COSO citation, all 3 non-CC EW slots have substantive text, EW[CC] empty

algorithm.step1_stem_clustering: Per section: compute stem Jaccard similarity (proper-noun-removed) between every pair of items. Group items with >90% similarity AND identical choice texts (positionally rotated) into template families.
algorithm.step2_rotation_verification: Within each family: verify CorrectChoice cycles through A→B→C→D→A (5-item groups) or A→B→C→D (4-item groups). If CC pattern is irregular → flag ROTATION_ANOMALY.
algorithm.step3_seed_selection: Evaluate each family member against canonical seed criteria: question_state='Unprocessed', EC >= 200 chars, EC contains ASC/COSO citation, all 3 non-CC EW slots substantive, EW[CC] empty. If exactly one member meets all criteria → designate as seed. If multiple → flag AMBIGUOUS_SEED. If zero → flag NO_VIABLE_SEED (requires re-authoring).
algorithm.step4_clone_marking: Non-seed family members marked as clones. Existing Archive status verified — if a clone was already Archived → verify correct. If a clone is Certified → flag CLONE_CERTIFIED (DL-012 learner-pool contamination).

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If section has <5 items → cannot form rotation group; all items flagged as standalone. If stem similarity is 70-90% (ambiguous) → flag BOUNDARY_UNCERTAIN for human review.
scans.blocking_rationale: Template rotation clones that reach certification boards waste reviewer effort. SOFT_BLOCK = clones cannot be certified until seed is identified and clones are either archived or given distinct content.
scans.false_positive_risk: LOW — >90% stem similarity threshold produces clean separation. Boundary items at 70-90% are flagged for human review. Integration with PG-011 TemplateFamily classification eliminates double-work.
scans.implementation_complexity: MEDIUM — Jaccard clustering is established (PG-011 reuses this). Seed criteria evaluation is straightforward property checks. ~100 lines total.

scans.title: Metadata Completeness and Consistency Audit
scans.purpose: Verify all items have complete required metadata per QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md. Detect missing, malformed, or mismatched metadata fields. Track metadata completeness across the entire pool.
inputs: Parsed question objects (AM-1) for all 5 packs + all 5 scored_cases files
QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md — required field definitions and validation rules
TAXONOMY_REGISTRY.md — controlled vocabulary enumerations
EXAM_BLUEPRINT.md — domain-to-section mapping

taxonomy_validation: question_state ∈ {Unprocessed, In Audit, Editorial Queue, Certified, Archived}
cross_field_validation: DifficultyScore matches Difficulty label per mapping (1=Easy, 2=Moderate-Easy, 3=Moderate, 4=Difficult, 5=Very Difficult)
Section tag aligns with BlueprintDomain if both present
ItemID format matches CaseID pattern for case items
explanation_completeness: No ExplanationWrong field has placeholder text (EV2)
algorithm.metadata_score: Compute per-item completeness as: (fields_present / fields_required) × 100. Per-section: mean of item scores. Per-pack: mean of section scores. Pool: weighted mean.

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If field is absent → count as missing (0% for that field). If field is present but invalid type → flag INVALID_TYPE. If taxonomy value is not in controlled vocabulary → flag TAXONOMY_VIOLATION. Missing fields do not block downstream scans but are reported.
scans.blocking_rationale: Metadata incompleteness degrades analytics and blueprint coverage reporting but does not create learner-safety risk. WARN = flag for metadata enrichment.
scans.false_positive_risk: LOW — field presence and type checks are deterministic. Taxonomy validation is deterministic against TAXONOMY_REGISTRY.md. Cross-field validation is deterministic.
scans.implementation_complexity: MEDIUM — Requires canonical list of required fields per question type. Requires taxonomy registry integration. Cross-field validation rules from QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md §5. ~120 lines.

scans.title: Certification Readiness Composite Score
scans.purpose: Produce a per-item certification readiness score aggregating ALL prior gate results. Gate certification decisions: which items can proceed to human CAQS §1.6 six-dimension review without structural or content defects.
inputs: Aggregated output from all prior gates (Gate -1 through Gate 4)
Per-item defect class inventory
Current question_state values

per_item.readiness_tier: CERTIFIABLE (score>=90, zero HARD_BLOCK) | CERTIFIABLE_WITH_DEFERRAL (score>=70, SOFT_BLOCK/WARN only) | BLOCKED (score<70 or any HARD_BLOCK) | IDENTITY_BLOCKED (Gate -1 failure) | PARSE_BLOCKED (Gate 0 failure)
blocking_defects: list of defect IDs preventing certification
warnings: list of WARN-level findings requiring attention

aggregate.by_defect_class_blockade: which defect classes block the most items

algorithm.scoring_formula: Base score = 100. Subtractions: HARD_BLOCK: -30 per violation. SOFT_BLOCK: -20 per violation. WARN: -10 per violation. IDENTITY_BLOCKED or PARSE_BLOCKED: score = 0 (automatic — no structural/content scores computed). Floor = 0. Ceiling = 100.
algorithm.certifiability_filters: CERTIFIABLE: score >= 90 AND zero HARD_BLOCK violations AND identity valid. CERTIFIABLE_WITH_DEFERRAL: score >= 70 AND zero HARD_BLOCK AND identity valid (SOFT_BLOCK/WARN defects deferred). BLOCKED: score < 70 OR any HARD_BLOCK. IDENTITY_BLOCKED: score = 0, identity invalid. PARSE_BLOCKED: score = 0, parse failed.
algorithm.defect_blockade_analysis: For each item with score < 90: enumerate blocking defects. Group by defect class. Identify which defect class resolution would unlock the most items → remediation prioritization.
algorithm.delivery_pool_filter: Items with readiness_tier = CERTIFIABLE AND question_state = 'Certified' → eligible for learner delivery pool. Generate pre-delivery exclusion list: all blocked items + all known-defective QIDs (DL-012 archive list).

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If any prior gate result is missing → mark item as READINESS_UNKNOWN (preceding gate must be run first). If score computation produces NaN → flag SCORING_ERROR.
scans.blocking_rationale: This is an aggregation scan, not a detection scan. It produces a composite readiness score to guide certification decisions but does not itself block certification — the underlying gates do.
scans.false_positive_risk: LOW — composite score is computed from deterministic gate results. No independent detection logic. Accuracy depends entirely on accuracy of upstream gates.
scans.implementation_complexity: LOW — Aggregation only. Scoring formula is simple arithmetic. Filters are boolean checks on accumulated defect inventory. ~60 lines.

scans.title: Registry Consistency — Cross-Reference and Integrity Verification
scans.purpose: Verify internal consistency of records against MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md and CURRENT_BASELINES.md. Detect drift between registry and source files. Verify no stale or phantom data in governance records.
inputs: All current AM-1 parsed item inventories (packs + cases)
MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md (generated, not hand-edited per governance-guard Rule 3)
CURRENT_BASELINES.md — hash baselines, certified counts
DEFECT_LIBRARY.md — open defect QID lists
SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-24.md — open risks and blocked file lists

algorithm.step1_registry_reconciliation: Extract all QuestionIDs from source files via AM-1 parse. Extract all QuestionIDs from MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md via parse. Compute symmetric difference. Flag: in-file-not-in-registry, in-registry-not-in-file.
algorithm.step2_baseline_verification: Compute SHA-256 hash of each pack file and case file. Compare to CURRENT_BASELINES.md §1 baselines. Flag any hash drift. Verify Certified count via AM-1 cross-check against baseline certified counts. Flag discrepancies > 1% tolerance.
algorithm.step3_defect_library_reconciliation: For each OPEN-status defect in DEFECT_LIBRARY.md: extract claimed QID scope. Cross-check against current AM-1 scan results: do the claimed affected QIDs actually show the defect as of current file state? Flag stale entries.
algorithm.step4_session_status_crosscheck: Cross-reference open risks in SESSION_STATUS against current AM-1 scan results. Flag resolved risks still listed as open. Flag NEW risks not in the session status.
algorithm.step5_delivery_pool_safety: Verify all items with question_state='Certified' pass: (a) zero HARD_BLOCK defects, (b) not on known-defective QID exclusion list, (c) identity valid. Flag any Certified item that fails any safety check.

scans.fail_safe_behavior: If registry file not found → flag REGISTRY_FILE_MISSING, skip Step 1. If baseline file not found → flag BASELINE_FILE_MISSING, skip Step 2. Each step is independent; failure in one does not block others.
scans.blocking_rationale: Registry inconsistency does not create learner-safety risk directly but indicates governance drift. WARN = flag for governance synchronization. HARD_BLOCK only for Step 5: Certified item with HARD_BLOCK defect in delivery pool.
scans.false_positive_risk: LOW — all checks are deterministic comparisons between parsed data from different sources. Hash computation is deterministic. QID symmetric difference is deterministic.
scans.implementation_complexity: MEDIUM — Requires parsing multiple file formats (registry .md, baseline .md, defect library .md). Step 5 requires integration with PG-001 through PG-005 defect inventories. ~180 lines.

dependency_graph.description: Scan dependency chain. Each scan depends on the output of prior scans and gates. Arrows indicate 'consumes output from'.

Gate_1.PG-001_DL008: Independent — runs on any parsed object
Gate_1.PG-009_EV8_CaseExtension: Depends on PG-001 (reuses same pass for MCQ)
Gate_1.PG-005_DL026: Shares AM-1 parse with PG-001. Co-detects DL-008 and DL-026 in same iteration
Gate_1.PG-004_DL016: Depends on PG-005 to cross-validate DL-026 flags against DL-016 status (reduces false positives)

Gate_2.PG-003_DL013: Independent — pure regex on ExplanationWrong fields
Gate_2.PG-AN-02_Metadata: Independent — field presence and taxonomy validation
Gate_2.PG-002_DL010: Depends on PG-004 (DL-016) to guard against wrong-target lexical overlap computation

Gate_4.PG-006_DL030: Tier 3 depends on PG-002 DL-010 EC-CC cross-check results; Tier 1 depends on PG-AN-02 metadata completeness

cross_gate_critical_path: PG-011 (Gate -1) → PG-010 (Gate 0) → AM-1 parse → shared object arrays → consumed by ALL downstream gates
PG-001 (Gate 1) → PG-002 (Gate 2) — DL-010 lexical overlap uses same Choices.{A,B,C,D} as DL-008 within-object extraction
PG-004 (Gate 1) → PG-002 (Gate 2) — DL-010 screening depends on DL-016 status to avoid wrong-target comparison
PG-004 (Gate 1) → PG-005 (Gate 1) — DL-026 cross-validation depends on DL-016 status artifacts
PG-AN-01 (Gate 3) → PG-AN-03 (Gate 5) — template family classification feeds into certification readiness scoring

scan_once_consume_many_architecture.description: Every scan produces an immutable CERTIFICATION_SCAN_ARTIFACT consumed by downstream consumers. No rescan is ever needed — scan results are stable, versioned artifacts.

artifact_schema.parse_methodology: AM-1 Function constructor parse per S725 §2 + S726 §3
artifact_schema.reproducibility: Running same scan version on same file hashes produces identical artifact

pipeline_execution.gate_order: Gate -1 → Gate 0 → Gate 1 → Gate 2 → Gate 3 → Gate 4 → Gate 5 → Gate 6

timing.parallel_optimization_note: Gates -1 and 1 are per-pack independent and can run in parallel across all 5 packs. Gate 3 requires cross-pack data (all 5 packs loaded). Gate 6 requires multi-file reconciliation. With 5 parallel workers for independent gates and sequential execution for cross-pack gates, total wall-clock ~2 minutes.

stop_conditions: Gate -1 IDENTITY_BLOCKED: any item without constructible identity → excluded from downstream gates, but pipeline proceeds for IDENTITY_VALID items
Gate 0 PARSE_FAILED: any pack file unparseable → entire pack excluded from all downstream gates
Gate 1 HARD_BLOCK items: excluded from Gate 2+ processing but pipeline proceeds for clean items
Gate 2 SOFT_BLOCK items: flagged for deferral; pipeline proceeds
Gate 3 HARD_BLOCK: duplicate compound keys or zero-seed families → pipeline stops at Gate 3 for affected families
Gate 4 SOFT_BLOCK items: routed to human review; pipeline proceeds

after_every_run: AM-1 Pack B DL-008 = 0 (gold standard test per S725 §6.2)
QID list included in every finding (FM-005 compliance)
Two independent runs produce identical counts and QID lists (S725 §4.5)
after_remediation: Pre-remediation gate scan → remediate → post-remediation gate scan → compare. Post-scan must show defect reduction; any increase is a regression (FM-006, DL-028).
